title: Market spectral analysis of narrow-domain LLM supply and buying signals
creator: Ivy Martinez
description:
Goal: produce an operationalized lens to detect emergent narrow-domain LLM suppliers and correlate those supply signals with early buyer intent so PM/Sales/Procurement can proactively engage or add fallback variants.

Scope:
- Surface time-series signals for ~60+ targeted narrow-domain models (legal, clinical notes, code assistants for verticals, specialized search vectors).
- Combine public telemetry (GitHub commits/releases, package downloads), pricing and availability scraping, cloud region latency listings, and internal sales/PO/procurement mentions to create a composite signal.
- Produce a spectral/time-frequency view (heatmap + event overlay) to identify bursts, slow builds, and cyclical patterns.
- Deliver dashboard, prioritized triggers, and a short playbook for sales and solutions engineering.

Why this matters:
- Many narrow-domain entrants surface quickly; we need early indicators to update model catalog, onboard compatibility tests, and prepare Dedicated/Private capacity.
- Proactively detecting buying signals reduces churn/risk when customers evaluate new domain models and helps price/offer fallback economics.

Non-goals: general consumer LLM landscape remapping, exhaustive global model list beyond the initial 60, or building new ingestion infra (we'll reuse telemetry pipelines and dashboards).
acceptance_criteria: Catalog CSV of >=60 narrow-domain models with metadata (architecture, quantization support, region availability, public repo link, first-seen timestamp)
Time-series spectral heatmap dashboard (Looker/Metabase) covering at least 12 months of signals or full available history with ability to filter by domain and region
Three prioritized procurement triggers (burst, adoption-slope, pricing-drop) with numerical thresholds and an alerting rule in the operational alerts channel
Playbook (one-pager) for Sales/Solutions describing actions per trigger and recommended fallback model bundles
steps: Define narrow-domain taxonomy and target model list (workshop with Research and Solutions)
Map signal sources and permissions (telemetry, procurement logs, public scraping, repo watches)
Build ingestion queries and sampling rules (reuse ENG telemetry pipelines where possible)
Create spectral analysis pipeline and visualization prototype
Validate signals against three historical customer adoption cases (post-mortem analysis)
Ship dashboard, alert rules, and playbook; run 2 knowledge-share sessions with Sales and Solutions
